general_information.Syllabus Name: Fundamental of Graphic design_Nguyên lý đồ hoạ cơ bản
general_information.Learning-Teaching Method: Lectures, Tutorials, Discussions, Laboratory work, Group, Seminars
general_information.Description: Description: This course provides an introduction to visual design for students and provides them with the basic knowledge of design, visual principles, and visual form of a composition of art. Students will be able to lay out the composition of art works, analyze, and evaluate the effect of design elements in each composition on human eyes. Through this course, students will gain the knowledge and skills necessary to develop concepts, manipulate materials, and apply art elements and design principles to create effective and appropriate visual works based on the learned knowledge and skills.
general_information.StudentTasks: 1. Class attendance is strongly encouraged. Attend at least 80% of class hours in order to be accepted to the final examination 2. Actively participate in class activities 3. Fulfill tasks given by instructor after class 4. Use their own laptop in class only for learning purpose 5. Read the textbook in advance 6. Access the course website (https://flm.fpt.edu.vn/gui/Home) for up-to-date information and material of the course.
general_information.Tools: Individual tools prepared by students: - Paper (size A3, A4). Sketching paper sheet (A3) - Color, pencil, eraser, brushes, back ink pen, art lines, markers - Paper knife, roll of paper tape, - Laptop - Digital graphic design tools - Drawing board.

description: Description: This course provides an introduction to visual design for students and provides them with the basic knowledge of design, visual principles, and visual form of a composition of art. Students will be able to lay out the composition of art works, analyze, and evaluate the effect of design elements in each composition on human eyes. Through this course, students will gain the knowledge and skills necessary to develop concepts, manipulate materials, and apply art elements and design principles to create effective and appropriate visual works based on the learned knowledge and skills.

learning_outcomes.CLO Details: Describe basic design and visual principles.
Explain how people communicate visually and how visual principles affect human eyes.
Apply the art elements and knowledge of design principles to construct basic visual art compositions of graphic design, with appropriate use of AI tools as supportive aids,
Analyze constructure in an art composition.
Create the learner's own work of art based on learned knowledge and skills, including using handicraft.
Demonstrate a positive attitude, a professional working style, and ethical awareness in the use of AI tools in design practice.

assessments.Question Type: - Students to collect specific natural elements to sketch a basic composition of natural objects. - Students sketch natural elements, and analyze the organic and geometric feature of the sketch. - Drawing a black and white piece of visual idea/concept to create a stylized image of the nature elements
assessments.Knowledge and Skill: Knowledge - Understanding of basic design and visual principles - Knowledge of how to analyze construction in art composition - Awareness of ethical considerations in using AI tools for reference, inspiration, or stylization. Skills - Observation & research skills natural elements closely. - Sketching and translating observed forms into basic compositions. - Simplifying natural forms into points, lines, and geometric or organic shapes.
assessments.Grading Guide: 1. Students follow instructor's guide and observe nature 2. Students collect/take a photographs of the natural elements, and sketch. 3. Defining and stylizing points, lines and geometric shapes from a natural elements to composition following instructor's guide. 4. Peer and instructor's review in class 5. Submit work in class
assessments.Note: Submission Files: 1. Word file containing all research and development steps including AI Usage Report (.docx/PDF) 2. Sketches in class (paper) 3. Submit the final work in class In-Class Work: 1. Presentation of research and sketches 2. Peer and instructor feedback on sketch, research, and stylizing idea. 3. Drafting and revising assignment during In-class sessions. 4. Submit the final work in class

assessments.Question Type: - Research the rhythm from everyday life. - Create black and white module using lines and geometric and organic shapes collected from assignment 1 - Make compositions with rhythm from modular.
assessments.Knowledge and Skill: Knowledge - Understanding of rhythm as a principle of design - Knowledge of how art elements (line, shape, form, space) can be organized into rhythmic structures. - Knowledge of modular composition techniques in graphic design. Skills - Create a repeatable visual unit from simple elements. - Arranging modules to form balanced, dynamic rhythmic designs. - Analyze how rhythm affects visual impact and viewer experience.
assessments.Grading Guide: 1. Students pick a part of geometric and organic shapes collected from assignment 1. 2. Using digital tools, rotate, locate and modify the chosen motif to create patterns with rhythm. 3. Peer and instructor's review in class 4. Submit work in class
assessments.Note: Submission Files: 1. Submit the final work in class (PDF) In-Class Work: 1. Peer and instructor feedback on sketch, motif and rhythm idea. 2. Drafting and revising assignment during In-class sessions. 3. Submit the final work in class

assessments.Question Type: - Using module from Assignment 2.1 to make compositions with different color schemes. - Practise mixing colors
assessments.Knowledge and Skill: Knowledge - Knowledge of color theory: hue, value, saturation. - Understanding of color harmony principles (complementary, analogous, triadic, split complementary, monochromatic). - Awareness of how visual principles (contrast, balance, emphasis, unity) affect the perception of color. Skills - Color mixing skills (manual blending or digital adjustments). - Application of color harmony to achieve aesthetic and functional outcomes.
assessments.Grading Guide: 1. Students pick patterns from assignment 2.1 2. Choose a colour palette based on colour harmony and apply to the chosen pattern. 3. Adjust value and saturation to create good visual effect. 4. Peer and instructor's review in class 5. Submit work in class
assessments.Note: Submission Files: 1. Submit the final work in class (PDF) In-Class Work: 1. Peer and instructor feedback on colour choices and adjustment. 2. Drafting and revising assignment during In-class sessions. 3. Submit the final work in class

assessments.Question Type: - Use geometric shape to make black and white compositions. - Composition must be satisfine related design principles
assessments.Knowledge and Skill: Knowledge - Understanding of design principles applied to black & white composition. - Knowledge of geometric abstraction in visual communication. - Awareness of how to use tools such as AI as a supportive tool in ideation. Skills - Arrange geometric shapes into effective visual design. - Create compositions align with design principles. - Use AI for exploration/inspiration while keeping originality.
assessments.Grading Guide: 1. Students sketch by hand composition following the instructor's guide. Students can use existing references or references created by AI 2. Adjust the composition according to the requirement of the assignment. 3. Apply shades of grey to create a greyscale composition. 4. Peer and instructor's review in class 5. Submit work in class
assessments.Note: Submission Files: 1. Word file containing all sketches and development steps including AI Usage Report (.docx/PDF) 2. Submit the final work in class (PDF) In-Class Work: 1. Peer and instructor feedback on composition choices and adjustment. 2. Drafting and revising assignment during In-class sessions. 3. Submit the final work in class

assessments.Question Type: - Tranfering the composition of Assignment 3.1 to color compositions unchange value. - Composition must be satisfine related design principles
assessments.Knowledge and Skill: Knowledge - Understanding of color theory (hue, saturation, value). - Knowledge of value preservation when applying color. - Understanding of how design principles hold across black & white and color. Skills - Converting monochrome to color without altering value hierarchy. - Design multiple color schemes while keeping compositional balance. - Technology -supported exploration skills - Digital drawing skills: precise, neat execution in color.

Choose numerous colour palette and apply to the chosen pattern while keeping the value of the black and white composition. 3. Present the work in a proper manner 4. Peer and instructor's review in class 5. Submit work in class
assessments.Note: Submission Files: 1. Submit the final work in class (PDF) In-Class Work: 1. Peer and instructor feedback on colour choices and adjustment. 2. Drafting and revising assignment during In-class sessions. 3. Submit the final work in class

assessments.Question Type: - Research theme - Research materials, test different textures on digital platforms and real materials to create special effects
assessments.Knowledge and Skill: Knowledge - Understanding of how textures and materials affect visual perception. - Knowledge of composition constructure (how texture interacts with form and space). - Awareness of visual communication principles through surface qualities. Skills - Research themes and materials. - Testing textures both digitally and manually. - Evaluating how textures contribute to composition structure. - Creative & craft skills: producing unique effects using real and digital media.
assessments.Grading Guide: 1. Students research theme and material. 2. Test different tactile of the same material. 3. Sketch and builde test 3d model digitally or by hand 4. Peer and instructor's review in class 5. Finish final model according to the instructor's requirement 6. Submit work in class
assessments.Note: Submission Files: 1. Submit the final work in class (physical model) In-Class Work: 1. Peer and instructor feedback on colour choices and adjustment. 2. Drafting and revising assignment during In-class sessions. 3. Submit the final work in class
